body.text: When does the Aegean olive harvest run (October–December)?

Across the North and South Aegean—from Ayvalık and Edremit down to Urla, Milas, and Datça—the olive harvest runs from early October through late December. Early-harvest (erken hasat) picking of still-green olives occurs in October and early November for high-polyphenol, grassy oils, while riper late-harvest picking continues into December for softer, fruitier yields.

Public harvest celebrations anchor the autumn calendar. In Balıkesir province, [Ayvalık's olive harvest route](https://goturkiye.com/routes/3-day-olive-harvest-route-in-ayvalik) comes alive in late October and early November with grove picking in Altınova and Küçükköy, open-air tastings, and press demonstrations. Farther south along the [Aegean Olive Tree Route](https://goturkiye.com/culturaljourneys/olive-tree-route), İzmir's Urla peninsula pairs autumn olive pressing with vineyard-to-table dining and mild daytime temperatures (typically 16–22°C), avoiding summer coastal crowds.
Can visitors tour cold-press mills and taste early-harvest oils?

Yes. Working modern two-phase cold-press mills (soğuk sıkım, pressed below 27°C) and heritage olive museums across Ayvalık, Küçükköy, and Urla welcome visitors by appointment during October and November. Tastings compare unfiltered ilk sıkım (first press) oils from regional cultivars such as Ayvalık (Edremit), Memecik, and Hurma olives.

On the Urla peninsula, history and production meet directly: ancient Klazomenai preserves a reconstructed 6th-century BCE olive-oil workshop, while the nearby [Köstem Olive Oil Museum](https://goturkiye.com/culturaljourneys/olive-tree-route) in Uzunkuyu traces 4,000 years of Anatolian pressing technology. In Ayvalık and neighboring Küçükköy, family-run boutique producers host guided grove walks and sensory tastings in blue tulip glasses, explaining acidity levels (extra-virgin must stay at or below 0.8% oleic acid), peppery finish, and proper dark-glass storage. Pair mill visits with [Urla's farm-to-table dining scene](https://goturkiye.com/routes/1-day-fine-dining-route-in-urla), where chefs showcase seasonal Aegean greens (otlar), artichokes, and wood-fired seafood dressed in the week's fresh press.

body.text: Which boutique farm hotels in Urla, Ayvalık and Datça offer harvest stays?

Small-scale vineyard and olive-estate properties across Urla, Ayvalık, and Datça host autumn stays built around grove walks, harvest breakfasts, and seasonal dinners. Options include stone countryside retreats around Küçükköy and Cunda in Ayvalık, chef-led vineyard-and-grove hotels in Urla, and dedicated hillside properties such as [Olive Farm Guest House](https://www.guesthouse.olivefarm.com.tr/en) in Datça.

Because autumn harvest weekends attract both Istanbul weekenders and culinary travelers, booking 6 to 8 weeks ahead is wise—particularly around the Ayvalık harvest festival and Turkish Republic Day (October 29). Renting a car from İzmir Adnan Menderes Airport (ADB) or hiring a private driver makes connecting rural mills, coastal towns, and hillside farms straightforward, as public buses rarely reach working olive presses.

items: Book working mill visits 1–2 weeks in advance; harvest crews operate on tight daily pressing schedules.
Pack closed-toe walking shoes and casual layers that can handle grove dust or brief autumn showers.
Taste oils neat before buying—look for harvest date labels (e.g., October/November 2026) rather than generic "best by" dates.
Request leak-proof metal tins or cushioned bottle sleeves if flying home with oil.
Reserve Urla's acclaimed farm-to-table dinner tables well ahead for Friday and Saturday nights.

body.text: What customs limits apply when flying home with olive oil?

Under [FAA PackSafe rules](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/oils) and [TSA liquid guidelines](https://www.tsa.gov/travel/security-screening/whatcanibring/items/oils-and-vinegars), nonflammable food oils like olive oil are restricted to 100 ml (3.4 oz) containers in carry-on bags, while larger bottles and metal tins are permitted in checked baggage. Always check your airline's weight limit and your destination country's personal-import allowance.

For customs entry, commercially sealed olive oil for personal use is generally admissible under [U.S. Customs and Border Protection agricultural guidelines](https://www.cbp.gov/travel/clearing-cbp/bringing-agricultural-products-united-states) (declare all food items on arrival). Travelers returning to the European Union or Great Britain should verify current personal-allowance and food-import guidance via [Your Europe](https://europa.eu/youreurope/citizens/travel/carry/meat-dairy-animal/index_en.htm) and [GOV.UK](https://www.gov.uk/bringing-food-into-great-britain), as non-EU plant-oil quantities must remain clearly for personal consumption rather than commercial resale. Metal 1-liter or 2-liter tins travel far more safely inside checked luggage than glass bottles; double-bag each tin inside heavy zip-lock bags wrapped in clothing.

faq.q: What is the best month for an Aegean olive oil harvest trip in Türkiye?
faq.a: Late October through mid-November offers the highest concentration of active cold-press mills, green early-harvest (erken hasat) tastings, harvest festivals in Ayvalık and Milas, and pleasant autumn weather.

faq.q: What is the difference between early-harvest and late-harvest Turkish olive oil?
faq.a: Early-harvest oil is pressed from green olives in October and early November; it yields less oil per kilogram but delivers bright grassy aromas, higher polyphenols, and a peppery throat finish. Late-harvest oil from darker olives in December is milder and rounder.

faq.q: Can I buy olive oil at Istanbul or İzmir airport duty-free to carry in the cabin?
faq.a: Yes, sealed duty-free bottles in tamper-evident security bags (STEB) can be carried in the cabin on direct flights, though if you have a connecting security screening abroad, liquids over 100 ml may still need to move into checked luggage.

faq.q: How many days should I spend on an Ayvalık and Urla olive oil route?
faq.a: Four to five days allows two days around Ayvalık, Küçükköy, and Cunda Island, followed by two to three days exploring Urla's mills, Klazomenai, Köstem Olive Oil Museum, and farm-to-table restaurants.

faq.q: Should I buy olive oil in glass bottles or metal tins for flying?
faq.a: Sealed metal tins (500 ml to 2 liters) are lighter, block light that degrades olive oil, and resist breakage far better than glass bottles inside checked luggage.

faq.q: Are working olive mills open to walk-in tourists?
faq.a: Some larger estates have tasting rooms with set hours, but many active cold-press mills run at full capacity during harvest and require advance appointments so visits do not interrupt pressing lines.
